analysis.title: Earnings Tracker Week 2: Bad AI vibes clouding good fundamentals
key_insights: After Week 2, 123 S&P 500 companies (30% of index earnings) have reported. 78% beat EPS expectations, versus 80% after Week 2 last quarter and a historical post-Week 2 average of 65%.
Reporters beat EPS by 2% in aggregate, or +6% excluding Meta's one-time litigation charge. Consensus 3Q EPS growth is still tracking 27% YoY.

Corporate sentiment in earnings transcripts cooled from 2Q's record high but remains elevated, and 'weak demand' mentions are well below average. Mentions of 'inflation' and 'cost pressures' are up 40% YoY.
The ratio of above- to below-consensus EPS guides is 1.6x month to date, down from 2.6x in July and above the October average of 1.0x. October has 21 above-consensus guides, 13 below and 22 neutral.
Upward revisions to 4Q and 2027 EPS estimates come entirely from Info Tech and Energy. Excluding Tech and Energy, 4Q EPS estimates are down 0.3% and 2027 estimates are down 0.1% month to date.

Meta fell 7% after saying it will 'continue investing aggressively' and may need to raise 'hundreds of billions' over several years. Lam Research fell 12% as supply constraints capped 4Q guidance roughly in line with consensus.

Info Tech has the strongest breadth of positive revisions of any sector, with nearly 5x more upward than downward 2027 EPS revisions month to date. Fears of an AI bust put the sector on pace for its worst month vs. the S&P 500 since DeepSeek in January 2025 (-5ppt month to date).

Earnings beats are not driving dispersion. Beaters outperformed by an average of 0.7ppt the next day (historical 1.0ppt), the same as misses, which usually underperform by 2ppt. The average one-day move is 3.7% vs. 5.3% in 2Q.

Factor rotation is out of Momentum and Growth and into Value and Cash Deployment, driven by AI anxiety, rate relief and higher oil. High FCF/EV leads all factors month to date at +11.4%, more than 15ppt ahead of the average Momentum factor.
Week 3 is the busiest week: 180 S&P 500 companies representing over a third of index earnings report, including Google and Microsoft (10/28) and Amazon (10/29). Focus is AI monetization vs. spending.
Hyperscaler (Meta, Google, Amazon, Microsoft, Oracle) 2027 capex estimates have been revised up nearly 90% YTD to over $1.1tn. Capex is expected to grow over 90% YoY in 2026 and slow to 40% in 2027.

Hyperscaler capex as a share of operating cash flow was 70% in 2025 and is expected to exceed 100% in 2026 through 2028. Hyperscaler free cash flow has dropped, which pulls down S&P 500 FCF relative to net income.
The gap between hyperscaler cloud revenue growth and capex growth is narrowing, with further upward capex revisions named as the risk.
S&P 500 capex grew 37% YoY in 2Q 2026, the strongest pace in BofA's data history. Ex-Tech and Mag 7, capex grew 11%, and 52% of CEOs expect higher capex over the next six months.
Meta's 2026 capex guidance was narrowed to $135-145B from $130-145B.

BofA card spending per household rose 6.2% YoY in September (5.1% ex-gasoline). 71% of retail categories posted positive transaction growth, and the top 5% income cohort grew fastest. Higher oil could take multiple quarters to dent spending, a downside risk to 4Q.
After the repeal of IEEPA tariffs the effective tariff rate has settled near 7%. BofA economists see risk of re-escalation if the midterms produce gridlock.
About $140B of IEEPA tariff refunds have been paid against an estimated $165B eligible (over 80%). Refunds are worth 0-5% of 2026 GAAP S&P 500 EPS depending on assumptions.
A stronger dollar cut 3Q sales growth by about 0.2ppt, reversing a 0.5ppt tailwind in 2Q and 2.0ppt in 1Q. Every 10% drop in the USD adds roughly 3ppt to sales growth.

Earnings quality is weaker. One-time investment mark-ups at Amazon and Google contributed nearly 20ppt to 2Q S&P 500 EPS growth (+50% reported, +32% excluding them). A reversal in valuations such as SPCX could hurt.
Consensus 2027 EPS growth is +16% vs. more than 30% for 2026. BofA forecasts +12% for 2027 and sees risks skewed to the downside.
Info Tech, and Semis within it, is expected to supply 79.7% of S&P 500 EPS growth in 2027 (Semis 62.6%).
BofA's 3Q26 S&P 500 EPS estimate is $93.50 (+32% YoY) vs. bottom-up consensus $90.45 (+27%). 2027 is $410 (+12%) vs. consensus $423 (+16%).
Consensus 3Q net margin expansion is 2.6ppt YoY for the S&P 500 ex-Financials but only 0.1ppt ex-Financials, TMT and Energy.
Small caps: 61 S&P 600 companies reported, 52% beat EPS, 36% beat sales. Mid caps: 52 S&P 400 companies reported, 60% beat EPS, 42% beat sales. Both have fewer beats than this point last quarter.
Russell 2000 3Q consensus EPS growth is +43% YoY aggregate and +8% median.

market_movers.rationale: Fell 7% after guiding 2026 capex to $135-145B, saying it will keep investing aggressively and may raise hundreds of billions of dollars over several years.
Fell 12% as supply constraints capped 4Q guidance roughly in line with consensus. Cleanroom space and component constraints persist into 2027.
Reports 10/28 with attention on AI monetization vs. spending. A possible revaluation hit on SPCX is flagged.

sector_views.rationale: Strongest revision breadth (nearly 5x more up than down for 2027 EPS) and the main source of 2027 EPS growth, but the sector is on pace for its worst month vs. the S&P 500 since January 2025 on AI cycle fears.
Energy and Tech supply all of the upward 4Q and 2027 EPS revisions. 3Q consensus EPS growth is 134.9% YoY.
Worst 2027 EPS revision breadth in October. Utilities and consumer sectors saw the weakest guidance trends.

earnings_insights: S&P 500 3Q26 consensus EPS growth is +27% YoY on the bottom-up basis (EPS $90.45), and +30.3% YoY on current constituents. BofA's own estimate is $93.50 (+32%).
78% of the 123 reporters beat EPS (reported, vs. consensus), 67% beat sales and 57% beat both. Aggregate surprise was +2% reported and +6% excluding Meta's one-time litigation charge.
Consensus 3Q26 EPS growth by sector (current constituents): Tech +66.4%, Semis +130.8%, Energy +134.9%, Communication Services +53.9%, Materials +30.5%, Industrials +15.6%, Health Care +0.4%.

Meta guided 2026 capex to $135-145B including finance lease principal payments. Its 14-C filing says forecasts showed a need to raise hundreds of billions of dollars over several years starting as early as fall 2026.
SpaceX said new compute deployments are generating a payback of less than a year at current pricing.
Texas Instruments reported broadening demand across Industrial, Automotive and Data Center. Lam Research said cleanroom space and supply-chain constraints will limit chipmakers into 2027.

United Rentals reported double-digit growth in power, metals and minerals. Capital One said credit is in a very good place. American Airlines reported premium unit revenue +18.5% YoY and managed corporate revenue +28%. Tractor Supply cited strength among Gen Z and millennial customers and rural stores.
Consensus 2027 EPS is $423 (+16%) vs. BofA $410 (+12%). 2026 is $365 (+33%) in both.
Consensus 3Q26 net margin for the S&P 500 ex-Financials is 15.0% (+2.6ppt YoY).
Week 3 reporting includes Visa and Coca-Cola (10/27), Alphabet and Microsoft (10/28), Amazon, Eli Lilly, Mastercard, Intel and Coinbase (10/29), and Exxon, AbbVie and Chevron (10/30).

macro_indicators.interpretation: Third strongest growth in four years, broad across categories. Consumer is resilient, though higher oil could dent spending over several quarters.
Settled after the IEEPA tariff repeal. Re-escalation risk if the midterms produce gridlock.
Worth 0-5% of 2026 GAAP S&P 500 EPS, with consumer and industrial companies citing it most.

macro_indicators.indicator: FX impact on S&P 500 sales growth
macro_indicators.interpretation: BofA estimate. The stronger dollar turned a 0.5ppt tailwind in 2Q into a modest headwind.
Risks skewed to the downside on rates, commodity pressure and AI capex durability.

macro_indicators.indicator: Labor share of US corporate operating costs
macro_indicators.interpretation: Wage inflation, which has been decelerating, is the main swing factor for index margins.

risk_factors: AI capex durability and monetization: hyperscaler capex above 100% of operating cash flow in 2026-2028 and the cloud revenue vs. capex growth gap narrowing.
Rising inflation and cost pressures, mentioned by 40% more companies YoY, against pricing power.
Higher oil and geopolitical conflicts denting consumer spending in 4Q.
Weaker earnings quality: one-time investment gains and low FCF conversion.
Deceleration of EPS growth from above trend historically coincides with the weakest equity returns (average 7.8% LTM return).
Supply-chain and cleanroom constraints limiting semiconductor equipment and chipmaker output into 2027.
charts_described: Exhibit 2 lists 3Q26E S&P 500 EPS at $90.45 (+27%) for bottom-up analysts and $93.50 (+32%) for BofA Strategy, and 2027E at $423 (+16%) vs. $410 (+12%).
Exhibit 31 shows hyperscaler capex of $793B (+91%) in 2026E and $1113B (+40%) in 2027E.
Exhibit 52 shows that when EPS growth is above trend and decelerating, average LTM S&P 500 return is 7.8% vs. 14.9% when above trend and accelerating (data since 1936).
vol_and_positioning: Momentum and Growth factors are being sold and Value and Cash Deployment bought month to date. High FCF/EV is up 11.4%, more than 15ppt ahead of the average Momentum factor.
Info Tech is on pace for its worst month relative to the S&P 500 since DeepSeek in January 2025 (-5ppt month to date).
Post-earnings moves are muted: the average one-day absolute move is 3.7% vs. 5.3% last quarter.
geopolitical: Higher oil from unresolved geopolitical conflicts is cited as a downside risk to 4Q consumer spending.
Geopolitical bottlenecks and a higher cost of capital could disrupt the AI-driven earnings story.
Possible trade tension re-escalation if the midterms lead to gridlock in Washington.

tension_points.bull_case: Positive EPS revision breadth in Info Tech is the strongest of any sector, with nearly 5x more upward than downward 2027 EPS revisions, and Meta says AI investments are already delivering substantial incremental advertising revenue.
tension_points.bear_case: Hyperscaler capex is expected to exceed 100% of operating cash flow in 2026-2028, 2027 capex estimates are up nearly 90% YTD, and fears that the AI boom paves the way for a bust have put Tech on pace for its worst month vs. the S&P 500 since January 2025.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further upward capex revisions that widen the gap over cloud revenue growth, flagged as the risk in Exhibit 34, would undercut the bull case.

tension_points.bull_case: Consensus expects 2027 EPS of $423 (+16%), with estimates revised well above historical trends and guidance net positive.
tension_points.bear_case: BofA forecasts $410 (+12%), sees downside skew from rates, commodities and geopolitics, and notes returns are weakest when EPS growth is above trend but decelerating.

theme_stances.key_argument: Index EPS remains highly dependent on the durability of the AI capex cycle and successful monetization, and a higher cost of capital and geopolitical bottlenecks could disrupt it.
